Prior review retained below:


Distinct challenge review on 2026-10-05 by the same Codex agent, not an independent human or second-agent review. Re-read all 240 literal statements against their numeric responses, unchanged agreement directions, axis briefs and counterevidence. Checked head-of-government questions against the prime minister rather than the monarch; retained the genuine constitutional-monarchy qualification for national leaders generally. Corrected immigration 01 and 09: administrative restriction does not imply the exact annual numerical mechanism. Corrected immigration 03 to reflect family immigrants rather than skills-only permanent residence and marked family reunification 04 as an estimate specific to the permanent-settlement class. Added the actual current 2023 rules PDF, independently read through text extraction. Read treaty rules sections 40 and 45: domestic withdrawal authority is qualified by treaty terms, not a universal international approval requirement. Added UNFPA programme implementation evidence, correcting the parental-veto estimate and improving inclusion evidence without asserting complete 2026 classroom implementation. Added one public-school prayer/dress example, explicitly local and older; revised religion teaching to a mixed response rather than claiming every school is purely descriptive. Rejected treating general selective trade barriers as proof of a specific anti-foreign-subsidy restriction. Reviewed every Neutral as a specified competing-institution assessment; none was chosen simply to replace an unknown answer. Country institutions, not citizen attitudes, are the target. Primary ministry sources share one government publisher; independent cross-checks include Freedom House, Bertelsmann, IMF, WTO and UN programme evaluation, with observation dates distinguished. Some official PDFs were accessible only through indexed excerpts or older versions, and their narrow use and lack of current consolidation are disclosed. AI strategy is adopted aspiration, not proof of completed deployment. The Ministry of Health listing is contextual, not a full brain-implant or enhancement regulation. No current autonomous-weapons, national-IQ, racial-violence, general healthy-person brain-implant, embryo-enhancement or precise novel-food policy is invented. Flag downloaded from observed Commons file link and visually inspected as a 900×600 PNG, 97,692 bytes; the linked file page records PD-Bhutan/public-domain status and contributor history. Scores were not targeted or copied from neighbors. All gaps covered by the owner’s educated-assumption rule are answered with explicit uncertainty. neutralAnswers.rationale: Educated assumption: Security clearances and monitoring coexist with constitutional privacy protections. This is a mixed assessment, not proof of multiyear innocent-person movement retention; duration and deletion rules remain unverified.

Educated assumption: Licensed civilian arms exist and security clearance is required, so a blanket ban is inaccurate. A general personal-defence entitlement based only on violence checks was not verified; licensing discretion and permitted ownership support a mixed response.

Educated assumption: Official calendars retain common Buddhist festivals while also recognizing Dassain and district celebrations; both common coordination and community accommodation are implemented. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Civic language, minority recognition and actual accommodation do not by themselves establish every migrant-specific cultural priority.

Educated assumption: Common dress expectations coexist with minority worship protections. No full-body-covering exception or general ban was verified; the mixed institutional context supports a conditional estimate rather than inventing a burqa rule.
Educated assumption: Defensive emphasis coexists with armed UN protection beyond defence of Bhutan or an ally, producing a genuinely conditional use-of-force assessment.

Educated assumption: Border security requires intelligence, while external cooperation and diplomatic restraint constrain provocation. No specific espionage-risk doctrine was established; these competing operational priorities support a mixed estimate.
Educated assumption: Domestic capacity support coexists with extensive essential imports from India; reserve-related restrictions do not prove a universal domestic-production preference.
Educated assumption: Farm support and biosafety regulation coexist with large food imports. Food-safety controls alone are not protection of farming capacity; the mixed assessment is conditional.

Educated assumption: State crypto mining and digital-bank initiatives coexist with national currency and financial controls. They do not demonstrate unrestricted private currency competition; both adoption and control justify a mixed estimate.

Educated assumption: The central bank has statutory monetary functions and manages macroeconomic constraints while supporting development priorities; this is a mixed estimate, not proof of direct government rate-setting.

Educated assumption: Private rental markets coexist with public affordable rents; nationwide current rent-control limits were not fully verified, so neither a wholly free nor wholly administered system is asserted.

Educated assumption: Progressive taxation and targeted assistance reduce some disparities, but limited cash-transfer coverage qualifies substantial disposable-income equalization. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Tax rates, actual cash eligibility and adequacy are distinct; public services and employer wages do not themselves establish cash redistribution.
Educated assumption: Kidu and public services support dignity but cash provision is limited. This mixed estimate weighs social participation objectives against uncertain benefit adequacy.

Educated assumption: Civil lawmaking and constitutional Buddhist ethos coexist; neither wholly religion-independent justification nor exclusively religious derivation describes the system. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Civil authority, faith accommodation and heritage practice may coexist; personal belief does not establish religion’s governmental role.

Educated assumption: Civil general education and religious-awareness objectives coexist with an actual public-school policy allocating prayer time and a religion committee. This mixed response reflects secular learning alongside formative religious practice; one school’s older policy does not establish every national curriculum or classroom.
Educated assumption: Green technology and hydropower investment coexist with conservation commitments; no exclusive priority over reducing consumption was established.
Educated assumption: Housing and transport investment coexist with permanent forest safeguards and protected areas; these implemented competing priorities warrant a mixed response.

Educated assumption: Structured early learning changes attention conditions while developmental differences are recognized. A mixed estimate is likelier for attention capacity than a confident exclusive causal ranking; no direct national comparison was found.

Educated assumption: Parenting recognizes child-specific development while supporting environmental intervention. Temperament is distinct from learned habits, making an interaction estimate likelier than claiming a measured predominance.
